statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail sits in the watch band and remains below the block threshold.
recommendation: Tail is 20% with the U.S. cash session complete and CME equity futures in the 17:00-18:00 ET maintenance halt, so no price path forms in the current hour. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the Friday data, Fed-speaker and quarterly-expiration cash open at 13:00-14:30 UTC. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes 1.73% higher with volatility crushed after the Fed hike; quarterly expiration follows on Friday
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,446.98, up 1.73%, inside a 29,305.90-29,494.95 cash range, recovering most of the decline that followed the Federal Reserve's 25 basis point increase to a 3.75%-4% target range on 16 September. That was the first increase since 2023 and the vote was unanimous; the statement described the action as supporting a timelier return to the 2% goal and flagged that further increases may be needed. NQ futures settled the session at 29,720.50, up 1.59%, in the upper part of a 29,247.75-29,793.25 range before the 17:00 ET halt. Cross-asset confirmation was constructive rather than stressed: the VIX fell 12.82% to 15.44, the 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.95% from 5.01%, and WTI crude slipped 1.31% to about $101.09 as Saudi Arabia rerouted exports through the Strait of Hormuz to offset the closed East-West pipeline. Latest-session breadth context showed all eight tracked megacaps and all seven tracked semiconductor names higher, led by memory and foundry moves. Today's U.S. data were firm, with initial jobless claims at 196K against a 207K consensus and the Philadelphia Fed index at 37.8. The path was a gap higher followed by a narrow 0.64% intraday grind that finished near the session high, which keeps Tail in the watch band, while the orderly character of the recovery and the broad volatility decay keep it below the block threshold. Stress eases to 44% but stays close to the elevated boundary because the underlying regime is unresolved: a war-driven energy shock, a central bank that has resumed tightening, a 10-year yield near 5%, public political pressure on the Fed, and Polish warnings of Russian drone strikes on NATO's eastern flank. Friday adds August Industrial Production at 13:15 UTC, a Federal Reserve speaker at 13:30 UTC and September quarterly expiration, which concentrates flow into the cash open and the close.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 20:00 UTC are fully covered by published Claude assessments. Tail ranged between 16% and 26%, peaking at 26% in the 13:00 UTC hour around the U.S. cash open and easing to 20-21% into the close. Stress fell monotonically from 72% to 45% as the post-Fed repricing resolved in an orderly way and volatility decayed. The dominant mode was recorded as trend-up for every hour from 07:00 UTC onward, reflecting a persistent but measured upside recovery rather than a disorderly one.
outlookSummary: The projected path holds 20-21% through the futures halt and the thin overnight hours, dips to 19% in the lowest-participation late-Asian hour, then rises with participation across the European morning. It reaches its only conditional block-band reading of 25% in the 13:00 UTC hour on Friday, which stacks August Industrial Production at 13:15 UTC, a Federal Reserve speaker at 13:30 UTC and the quarterly expiration cash open at 13:30 UTC. It eases through the U.S. afternoon before a second conditional step to 24% in the 19:00 UTC witching hour, when quarterly expiration flow concentrates into the close. Stress tracks the same shape between 42% and 53%. Every forecast hour beyond the current one describes conditional risk, not observed structure.

forecast.analysis: Globex reopens at 22:00 UTC. The first prints after the halt are thin and can gap on repositioning without offering the two-sided flow mean reversion needs. Tail is held one point above the halt hour for that reopening-liquidity effect, not for any structure observed yet in this window.

Reopening gap risk after a +1.59% NQ session is a conditional checkpoint
No live price path is observable for this hour at assessment time

forecast.analysis: Pre-Tokyo hour. Conditional risk is that the reopening drift extends without retracement while depth is still thin. An orderly hold inside the prior session's upper range would be the benign case and would keep Tail in the lower watch band.
drivers: Asian pre-open liquidity remains thin before Tokyo
Checkpoint: whether the reopen holds inside the 29,247.75-29,793.25 range
Persistent backdrop: Fed moved to a 3.75%-4% target range on 16 September

forecast.analysis: Tokyo opens into the first full Asian pricing of the Fed's 25bp increase and of a 10-year yield near 4.95%. A conditional one-point step up covers cross-market repricing; this is anticipated participation risk, not observed structure, and generic event weight is carried mainly in Stress.

10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.95% from 5.01%

news.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement (16 September 2026)

forecast.analysis: Asian morning. If Tokyo prices the hike without a directional break, two-sided flow normally returns and Tail steps back down. The conditional risk is an aligned regional follow-through that extends the U.S. move rather than consolidating it.
drivers: Asian morning typically restores two-sided flow after the cash open
Invalidation: a sustained regional break beyond the overnight range
Volatility decay from a 15.44 VIX close supports mean reversion

forecast.analysis: Mid-Asian session. On the base case the overnight range consolidates and realised volatility stays compressed after the 12.82% VIX decline, which is the environment where retracement is most reliable. Tail returns to the lower watch band on that assumption.
drivers: Mid-Asia hours are typically the quietest of the 24-hour cycle
VIX at 15.44 is consistent with compressed overnight realised volatility
Assumption: no new geopolitical headline enters the tape

forecast.analysis: China and Hong Kong mid-session. Conditional risk stays low absent a regional catalyst. The persistent overhang is the Iran-war oil complex, with WTI near $101, which can reprice Asian risk appetite on a supply headline at any hour.
drivers: Greater China session rarely drives the Nasdaq-100 directly
WTI near $101.09 keeps an energy-driven inflation channel open
Saudi East-West pipeline outage remains unresolved supply context

forecast.analysis: Late Asian trade into the European pre-open is usually the lowest-participation hour of the cycle. On the base case of a quiet overnight, conditional Tail falls just below the watch band for this single hour; any overnight headline would invalidate that assumption.
drivers: Lowest-participation hour of the overnight cycle on the base case
Invalidation: an overnight geopolitical or energy headline
Conditional mapping returns to the lower band only for this hour

forecast.analysis: European pre-open. Positioning ahead of the cash open begins to add directional flow, and Friday is a quarterly expiration, so early European hedging flow can be heavier than usual. Tail returns to the watch band as a conditional participation effect.
drivers: European pre-open positioning restores directional flow
18 September is September quarterly (quadruple witching) expiration
Expiry-related hedge adjustment can begin in European hours

forecast.analysis: European cash open. Conditional risk is a gap continuation of the U.S. recovery that European participants extend without a meaningful pullback. The benign alternative is the more common one after a vol-crush session: an opening range that mean-reverts inside the overnight band.
drivers: European cash open adds the session's first large liquidity step
Checkpoint: whether the opening range holds inside the overnight band
Persistent driver: Fed signalled further increases may be needed

forecast.analysis: European morning. Sovereign bond trade is the channel to watch: yields backed off after touching the highest 10-year level since 2007, and a renewed rise would pressure long-duration tech. Absent that, the hour is expected to be two-sided.
drivers: European sovereign yields are the main transmission channel this hour
10-year Treasury retreat from about 5.01% is a supportive condition

forecast.analysis: Mid European morning, with expiration-related flow building in index products. Conditional risk is pinning-driven drift rather than a trend break. Pinning usually helps mean reversion, so this stays in the watch band rather than above it.
drivers: Quarterly expiration flow builds through the European morning
Option pinning typically supports, not denies, mean reversion
No U.S. macro release is scheduled in this window

drivers: European midday is a recognised low-participation window
Assumption: expiry flow stays balanced this early in the session
Conditional easing depends on a quiet overnight and European morning

forecast.analysis: Final quiet hour before U.S. premarket. Conditional risk stays in the lower watch band. Confidence steps down gradually across the forecast because live price-path evidence for hours this far out cannot exist at assessment time.

Confidence decays with distance from the assessment cutoff

forecast.analysis: U.S. premarket build on a quarterly expiration day. Index-level positioning ahead of the 13:15 UTC Industrial Production release and the cash open adds directional flow. Stress steps up on event proximity while Tail moves only one point, per the rule that event weight is not by itself path evidence.

August Industrial Production is scheduled for 13:15 UTC
Event proximity raises Stress ahead of Tail by design

forecast.analysis: Last premarket hour. Conditional dispersion widens into the stacked 13:00-14:00 UTC window, which contains the data release, a Federal Reserve speaker and the expiration-day cash open. Tail rises modestly; the larger step is in Stress.
drivers: Final hour before a stacked data, speaker and cash-open window
Expiration-day opening auctions carry larger-than-usual size
Forecast dispersion raises Stress more than Tail before a print

forecast.analysis: The stacked hour: August Industrial Production at 13:15 UTC, a Federal Reserve speaker at 13:30 UTC and the quarterly expiration cash open at 13:30 UTC. That combination on an already aligned upside regime is the documented failure mode for reverse and grid exposure, so conditional Tail crosses the block threshold for this one hour.
drivers: Industrial Production 13:15 UTC and Fed speaker 13:30 UTC
Quarterly expiration cash open at 13:30 UTC with SOQ-related flow

forecast.analysis: First full hour after the expiration open. Conditional risk is that the opening direction extends on shallow pullbacks; the benign case is the post-auction two-way trade that normally follows a settled expiration. Tail steps back inside the watch band but stays at its upper edge.
drivers: Post-open continuation versus retracement is the decisive checkpoint
Shallow-pullback extension would be the invalidating pattern

forecast.analysis: Late U.S. morning. By this point the session's direction is usually established and the expiry imbalance is largely absorbed. Conditional Tail eases on the assumption that price discovery after the data and the open has been orderly.

Assumption: orderly price discovery after the 13:30 UTC open

forecast.analysis: Early U.S. afternoon. Conditional risk stays in the lower watch band while closing-auction imbalance indications are not yet published. This is the calmest part of an expiration-day U.S. session on the base case.

forecast.analysis: The witching hour, 15:00-16:00 ET. Quarterly futures and options expiration concentrates flow into the close and closing-auction imbalances can produce a directional push with little retracement. Conditional Tail steps to the upper watch band for this structural window.
drivers: Quadruple witching flow concentrates in the final hour of cash trade
Closing-auction imbalances can drive a low-retracement push
Structural, scheduled liquidity event rather than a news shock

forecast.analysis: Expiration settles at the 20:00 UTC cash close and the weekly cycle ends. Conditional risk eases as the imbalance clears, though post-close futures trade into the weekend carries headline gap risk from the Iran-war energy complex and the eastern-flank NATO warnings.
